answer: Trust transfers at one timestamped moment: T, the block time when a peer's attestation signature lands on-ledger. That signature binds epoch, seed, and answer into a single attestation ID; the ledger refuses any second signature bearing that same ID, so identical trust cannot move twice. A sybil swarm may bloom like a meadow, yet each forged cipher fails the signature check, and every fresh ID must lock stake — a river of burned capital that drowns cheap fakes.
